question.text: What is the primary difference between a Direct Plan and a Regular Plan of the same mutual fund scheme?

answer.text: Direct Plans have a higher NAV at launch compared to Regular Plans
Direct Plans have a lower Total Expense Ratio (TER) as no distributor commission is included
Direct Plans invest in different securities than Regular Plans of the same scheme
Direct Plans are available only to institutional investors while Regular Plans are for retail investors

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook page 166, investors can go through distributors or directly through the AMC. Per page 177, Direct Plans exclude distribution expenses and commission and therefore have a lower TER, while Regular Plans have a higher expense ratio because distribution costs are accounted for. Both plans of the same scheme invest in the same underlying portfolio. The Trap: Option A is wrong because both plans typically start at the same NAV at launch (page 170 supports the Rs. 10 NFO face value); the NAV divergence is a consequence of the TER difference over time, not the launch position. Option C contradicts the identical-portfolio principle. Option D invents an investor-type restriction that does not exist. Note: The TER difference compounds over time, so the Direct Plan's NAV will tend to grow faster than the Regular Plan's for the same scheme, despite identical portfolios.
